tensions: The whole portfolio is +32% on borrowed momentum from one regulatory headline. Dominance at 58.5% is a single bad session from the 60% line that forces us out of everything. Meanwhile buying power is $3.62 — we are fully deployed with zero optionality, so the only way to act on any new signal is to kill something we already own. ADA is the designated sacrifice, but selling a position on the day it rips 8.7% is exactly the timing error that looks smart in a spreadsheet and dumb in a P&L. NEAR and ZEC are 40% of the book and both are extended; if privacy and AI narratives roll over together, the +32% becomes +10% in a week and there is no cash to average into the wreckage.

opening.text: BTC through $80,695, up 5.2%, and the SEC's innovation exemption did it — five years of tokenized stock trading waved through on the 17th. Dominance sits at 58.5%, under our 60% kill-switch, which means alts get to breathe. F&G 56. Greed, but not the stupid kind yet.

NEAR is the whole story: +47.5% in twelve days on confidential perps over Hyperliquid and $70M confidential TVL. It is overbought and I do not care. The rule is no trimming. We do not clip a 47% winner to feel clever — we let it run or we get stopped out honest.

ZEC +41% but it printed 1519 at midnight and gave back to 1481. ARB did the same thing harder — 0.226 overnight to 0.2085 now, so yesterday's entry is barely green despite CoinGecko's +24% headline. Overnight spikes that fade before New York wakes up are liquidity, not conviction. Watch both.

ADA is the problem. Fourteen days, +3.2%, while the book did +32%. It rose 8.7% today on pure beta — no news, no catalyst, just the tide. Sell order is pre-validated at $102.41 but it does not fire into a green candle. If ADA loses 0.215 or fails to make a new high by the next scan, it funds something better. XRP at -5.3% is the other laggard, but it is only four days old and gets its window.
